data.title: Maternal Sirolimus Therapy for Fetal Extensive Lymphatic Cystic Malformation: Selection Criteria, Management, and Outcomes in a Series of Six Cases
data.authors: Guibaud L; Bordas-Fournel M; Cabet S; Le Vaillant C; Bruel A; Lefran‡ois T; Megier C; Benachi A; Sohier M; Gallois Y; Somon T; Jouannic J-M; Canaud G; Guilhem A; Atallah A; Fraissenon A

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Maternal rapamycin (sirolimus) therapy for extensive fetal lymphatic malformations. Prenatal mTOR inhibition feasible with partial/marked lesion regression in 5/6 newborns; transplacental transfer observed. Observational case series (n=6); confounding by indication not excluded.
data.abstract_excerpt:
Maternal sirolimus therapy has emerged as a potential prenatal treatment for extensive fetal lymphatic malformations, particularly when associated with the risk of neonatal airway compromise. Data on prenatal indications, pharmacokinetics, and outcomes remain limited. We aimed to describe patient selection, treatment management, maternal and fetal safety, and early outcomes.

Between December 2023 and May 2025, 15 fetuses with extensive cystic or mixed vascular anomalies suggestive of lymphatic malformations were referred to a national reference center.
